newsitem.title: CHINA: China shipping 87,500T corn to S.Korea in Aug, Sep.
newsitem.headline: China shipping 87,500T corn to S.Korea in Aug, Sep.

text.p: China will load 87,500 tonnes of corn to ship to South Korea in August and September at a CIF (cost, insurance and freight) cost of $140.20 and $143.35 a tonne, China Economic Times said on Wednesday.
Two lots totalling 49,000 tonnes were loaded for South Korea in June and August, the newspaper said, without detailing the price.
Corn exported to Malaysia totalled 25,000 tonnes, loaded in April at a CIF cost of $150 a tonne, it said.
China decided to export corn in a bearish domestic market in the hope that falling prices could be reversed, it said.
Customs figures show China's corn exports soared by 11,920.5 percent in the first half of 1997 compared with same 1996 period, to 2.01 million tonnes.
China halted corn exports in late 1994 amid shortages that saw domestic prices soar. China had previously exported around nine to 10 million tonnes a year.

A good harvest last year coupled with the lack of exports led to oversupply and full warehouses in the northern production areas, with around six million tonnes already shipped to consumption regions in the south.
Traders have said China's total corn exports for 1997 could top 2.5 million tonnes.
Corn was quoted FOB (free on board) in the northern port of Dalian last week at $100/105 a tonne.
South Korea has been the major buyer of the Chinese corn, with some going also to the Philippines and Malaysia.
